MOMENTUMACCELERATIONCONTINUATION_LONG_KI.gate_a_result: FAILED TO RUN -- HorizonLabError: HYBRID FAST CONTROL PARITY FAILED (rows expected=2817 actual=2429).
MOMENTUMACCELERATIONCONTINUATION_LONG_KI.root_cause_diagnosis: This edge's candidate_events.py computes its calendar-time Event_Vol (_add_event_vol) over the FEATURES frame AFTER dropping rows with any NaN in required momentum-acceleration columns (Trend_Slope_Raw, Acceleration_Rank, etc.), not over the full raw bar grid. shared/research/v3_horizon_lab.py's hybrid-fast-grid control-parity check recomputes Event_Vol independently via calendar_time_event_vol against the FULL raw bar grid (_hfg_load_bars -> runtime._load_asset_bars()). Confirmed via direct debug: persisted Event_Vol at the 307 'dropped' event timestamps is valid/finite (~0.009-0.013), bars are unique/monotonic (no duplicate-timestamp bug), and all event Datetimes are exact bar-grid points -- so this is NOT a bar-loading or timestamp-alignment bug in the shared script. The divergence is specifically that NASDAQ's momentum/regime features have scattered mid-series NaN gaps (unlike US500's, where this same code apparently never produced a mismatch large enough to fail parity) which silently shifts the effective 4-hour lookback window used inside candidate_events.py's own vol computation relative to a true full-bar-grid calendar lookback.
MOMENTUMACCELERATIONCONTINUATION_LONG_KI.disposition: NOT a shared-script bug to patch (v3_horizon_lab.py's recompute against the full bar grid is the methodologically correct behavior; the edge's own vol computation silently deviating from a true full-grid calendar lookback whenever features have NaN gaps is the edge-specific quirk). NOT patching the edge's vol computation either, since that would change established geometry mid-exploration (forbidden per feedback_edge_geometry_change_full_workflow -- edits before Gate A/B/C exploration is finished corrupt the parity reference). KILLED for NASDAQ: abandon this mechanism here, move to next priority mechanism (explosiveregimecontinuation_long). Folder kept on disk per the universal no-delete policy, never promoted to edge_universe.json.

EXPLOSIVEREGIMECONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_.root_cause: SAME PATTERN as MOMENTUMACCELERATIONCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BUG_2026-10-02: candidate_events.py/_normalize_feature_input() drops rows with any NaN in required feature columns (here, SADF_ct_50 and related regime columns) BEFORE _add_event_vol() computes the calendar-time Event_Vol via calendar_time_event_vol(). This makes the 4-hour lookback run over a non-contiguous, feature-availability-dependent bar subset rather than the true full calendar bar grid, so the independent Gate A reproduction (which recomputes over the full bar grid) cannot reproduce the persisted model rows. Confirmed this is a SHARED TEMPLATE PATTERN (same _normalize_feature_input -> _add_event_vol structure) likely present across several of the 12 US500-ported mechanisms -- worth expecting this failure mode to recur on others that require derived regime/momentum feature columns with scattered NaN gaps on NASDAQ specifically.

THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BU.thesis: Bullish thrust bar -> long momentum-ignition continuation. Retried on NASDAQ (cost_bps=1.12) as Attempt 6.
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BU.gate_a_result: FAILED TO RUN -- HorizonLabError: HYBRID FAST CONTROL PARITY FAILED (rows expected=4683 actual=4132).
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BU.root_cause_CORRECTED: Initially hypothesized this was the SAME Event_Vol-filtering bug as momentumaccelerationcontinuation_long/explosiveregimecontinuation_long, since this mechanism also required a derived feature column (ATR_14) before vol computation. DISPROVEN by direct check: ATR_14 is clean on NASDAQ (NaN only in the 14-bar warmup, zero NaN thereafter across all 66605 bars). Instrumented debug of the full chain instead found: 5125 events -> 4987 survive vol-attach (138 dropped, vol lookback is only 1hr/span50 for this edge, mostly fine) -> 4684 of those are in valid_feature_times (303 legitimately excluded for schema-feature NaN, not a bug) -> but materialize_horizon only returns 4132 rows, a further ~552-row drop with NO corresponding drop in model_rows.py own self-test stats (which only dropped 1 for horizon + 10 ambiguous-same-bar, nowhere near 552). This means the generic shared compute_first_touch_paths/materialize_horizon functions apply SOME additional eligibility filter beyond valid_feature_times that model_rows.py's own bespoke triple-barrier code does not apply (exact mechanism not yet isolated -- candidates include different same-bar PT/SL tie-break handling, since this edge's self-test shows unusually frequent ambiguous_same_bar/fallback_resolved events, or a stricter deadline-within-history requirement).
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BU.significance: This is the THIRD distinct manifestation of HYBRID FAST CONTROL PARITY FAILED on NASDAQ in 7 attempts (momentumaccelerationcontinuation_long, explosiveregimecontinuation_long, now thrustcontinuation_long) -- each with a different specific row-count divergence source, but all stemming from the shared Gate A tool's independent recompute disagreeing with each edge's own bespoke model_rows.py labeling by a meaningful margin (8-17%). No single root cause confirmed across all three. FLAGGED to the user as a cross-cutting finding rather than silently patched, since it touches shared production tooling (v3_horizon_lab.py) used across all assets, not just this one edge.
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_PARITY_BU.disposition: KILLED for NASDAQ (tooling-blocked, not an economic kill). Folder kept on disk.

THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_FULL_JOURNEY_202.summary: NASDAQ (cost_bps=1.12) Attempt 6. Bullish thrust bar -> long momentum-ignition continuation. The furthest any NASDAQ attempt got this session -- cleared Gates A/B/C/PBO and the full Step01-09 training pipeline, but FAILED Gate D.
journey: Self-test + export: PASSED (4683 model rows at default geometry H1_E50/V4h/PT2/SL1).

Gate A: initially FAILED with HYBRID FAST CONTROL PARITY (rows expected=4683 actual=4132) -- traced to a confirmed bug in shared/research/v3_horizon_lab.py: 5 call sites used pd.DatetimeIndex.asi8 without normalizing to nanosecond unit first; on venv312 bars are datetime64[us]-dtype so .asi8 returned MICROSECONDS, making every calendar-time hour-based lookback/horizon ~1000x too wide (4h became ~166 days). Same root cause explained the earlier momentumaccelerationcontinuation_long and explosiveregimecontinuation_long parity failures too. FIXED (user-approved) by adding .as_unit("ns") at all 5 call sites, matching the fix already present in every edge model_rows.py.
Gate A re-run after fix: PASSED cleanly. Best gross_mean_R=0.0578, 7/36 cells cleared the 0.05 kill bar.

Gate C (7 finalists, exact bid/ask replay): 3/7 positive exec_mean_R. Best: H20_E200_V10_PT1_SL1 (EVENT_VOL_LOOKBACK_HOURS=20, EWM_SPAN=200, VERTICAL_HORIZON_HOURS=10, PT=1, SL=1), exec_mean_R=+0.0238.
PBO (fixed rule, compound_velocity_stat): PBO=40.3% (<50% pass), Prob[OOS<=0]=5.8% (<50% pass). PASSED cleanly, better than most of the 12 live edges.

Winning geometry locked into candidate_events.py/model_rows.py/edge.yaml. Re-exported: 4681 model rows, re-ran Task 2A (build_mldp_executable_targets.py, newly (re)discovered prerequisite -- 100% resolution coverage, mean R=+0.038).
Step 01 (feature surgery): PASSED. F1=0.636, 156/156 candidate features kept (no negative-MDA clusters).
Step 02 (Optuna training): PASSED. Best CPCV F1=0.704.
Step 03 (OOF predictions): PASSED but raw ROC AUC=0.5095 -- a weak, near-coin-flip warning sign flagged at the time.

Step 03b/04/04b/05/06/07/08/09: ALL PASSED cleanly (Step05: 31/31, Step06: 8/8, Step07 smoke test approved, Step08 replay audit: 11 pass/1 warn/0 fail with ZERO replay diffs, Step09: deployment_status=PASS, deployable=True).

GATE D: FAILED. AUC=0.5095, p=0.1299 (one-sided Mann-Whitney, alpha=0.05) -- no statistically significant discrimination between true-positive and true-negative raw probabilities. Diagnostic Kendall tau (raw_probability vs realized_r) also near-zero (0.0045, p=0.64).
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_FULL_JOURNEY_202.interpretation: The underlying thrust-continuation EVENT (bar-level trigger + winning barrier geometry) has real, PBO-clean positive expectancy in backtest (gross_mean_R=0.058, exec_mean_R=0.024, PBO=40%). But the META-LABELING MODEL trained on top of it (predicting WHICH thrust events will win vs lose, using the 156-feature schema) has essentially no discriminative power -- AUC barely above 0.5, not significant. This means the edge as currently defined has no real way to filter good thrust events from bad ones beyond the base rate; it is economically interesting as a raw signal but not deployable as a trained meta-labeled edge in its current form. A plain unconditional strategy (take every signal) would reproduce the backtest result, but that is not how this project deploys edges (meta-label filtering + calibrated probability threshold is required by the pipeline).
THRUSTCONTINUATION_LONG_FULL_JOURNEY_202.disposition: KILLED for NASDAQ, but a genuine, informative, non-tooling kill -- the furthest any NASDAQ mechanism got this session. Folder kept on disk, deployable=True in its own manifest is misleading in isolation (Step09 checks internal pipeline consistency, not Gate D) -- NOT promoted to config/edge_universe.json, NOT run through promote_edge_status.py or portfolio_allocator per explicit instruction to stop and report before any further action.

GATE_C_EXTRA0_RERUN_2026-10-14.procedure: Replay ALL Gate-B-positive cells (net_mean_R>0 in the edge's original Gate A/B grid at 1.12 bps) with exact Bid/Ask, extra 0, delay 0 ms, --save. PBO/CSCV s=16 on daily-prorated log(1+0.01*exec_r) with compound_velocity_stat; PASS = PBO<0.5 AND Prob[OOS<=0]<0.5. Survivors -> geometry lock -> self-test -> export -> Task 2A -> Steps 01-09 -> Gate D.
